tasks.task: Write a risk-ranked test plan and test cases

items.when: When you have a spec, stories or screens and need numbered cases ranked by risk
When a feature is about to be built or a build is ready on staging, to run the whole cycle
Before the cases, to decide what to test at unit, API and browser level and where the gaps are
When you have user stories and need scenarios with a starting state, steps and expected result
When the spec covers only the happy path, to list the odd cases, smallest first
When the plan assumes users and systems behave, to ask what happens when they do not

tasks.task: Turn a complaint or failure into a bug report

items.when: When you have a complaint, screenshot or failed test and need a report a developer can act on
When the report is vague, to get repeatable steps, a minimal case and what proof is missing
When you have logs or a stack trace and the report must go in as a GitHub issue
When the evidence shows customer data, to draft the issue and list what to remove first
Before you attach a screenshot, to mask emails, phone numbers, keys and IDs on your own machine
When you have the repo, to make a repeatable failing case and record what is verified

tasks.task: Write acceptance tests from a spec or user story

items.when: When you have a spec or story and want pass or fail checks anyone can run before it ships
When the checks need full scenarios with set-up data, not one-line pass rules
When the build is done, to mark every requirement pass, fail or not run with what is left

tasks.task: Write manual test cases for a form or flow

items.when: When a sign-up, booking or checkout form needs a table of cases, including odd inputs
When you want more boundary and empty-value cases than the first table gave
When the page is built, to find buttons and controls that do nothing when used

tasks.task: Write unit tests for pasted code

items.when: When you need tests from a case table of rules, boundaries and errors, at the right level
When the function is tricky, to write its rules and edge cases down before any test
When the code has no tests, to get unit, linked-part and user-task tests with a coverage report
When a new rule or fix should start from a failing test and move in small steps
When the code is Python, to prove the tests fail when the change is broken on purpose
When tests are large and brittle, to list the cases and take one small step at a time
When you have the repo and want the tests written, run and fixed in the project itself

tasks.task: Write end-to-end browser tests for a key flow

items.when: First, to pick the few flows worth a browser test and push the rest down a level
When you have a user story or page and want Playwright tests you can run
When the suite is Cypress or needs a CI setup along with stable tests
When the tests are written, to check each against common bad habits such as fixed waits
When the flow must work on several browsers and phones, to run it on each and report

tasks.task: Write API test cases and test code

items.when: When you have an OpenAPI file, endpoint list or route code and want cases below the screen
When you have the API spec and need a plan covering sign-in, edge and failure cases
When you have the code, to get integration tests and fixtures for each route
When other teams or apps call the API, to catch breaking changes before they ship
When the tests live in a Postman collection and should run on every push

tasks.task: Triage a list of reported bugs

items.when: When a pile of reports needs severity, priority, duplicates and a next step for each
When the bugs sit in a GitHub repo, to sort and check each open issue and write it up
When bugs arrive as support tickets, to set a category, a priority and any known duplicate

tasks.task: Review a fix and list what to re-test

items.when: When a developer says a bug is fixed and you must decide what to test again
When you have the change and the tests, to mark each new behaviour covered or not
When the fix may treat a symptom, to see the cause proven with evidence first
When you can read the change, to review it for bugs, security and missing tests

tasks.task: Build the regression checklist for a release

items.when: When you ship on a schedule and need a short, ranked list to re-test after every change
When you have the repo, to rank missing, weak and stale tests by the behaviour at risk
When the release is a website, to run a smoke, standard or full pass and list the problems

tasks.task: Run release sign-off and give a go or no-go

items.when: Every release, weekly or per sprint, or before a big launch
When the test run is in, to group failures by cause and get a go or no-go call
When earlier QA says all clear, to check each claim against proof before sign-off
When the release changes behaviour users read about, to find test gaps and stale docs
When the release touches several systems, to check the joins between them and what fails first
When nobody has written how to undo the release or how to tell that it worked

tasks.task: Diagnose and clean up flaky tests

items.when: When a test passes and fails on the same code, or the suite is retried until green
Monthly, or at once when the team starts ignoring red builds
When one Playwright test is flaky, to find the cause and make the fix
When the suite is Cypress, to find fragile waits and old calls and fix the tests they hit
When the suite is Python, to list weak, flaky, slow and useless tests
When the whole suite is red, to fix and re-check in capped rounds until green or stopped

tasks.task: Test a page or flow for accessibility

items.when: When a page, flow or release needs an automated scan plus keyboard and screen reader checks
When you have the page or its code, to get ranked problems against the current standard
When you need findings tied to each rule and a test plan for keyboard and screen reader
When the site is checked every quarter, to rank new gaps and confirm last quarter's fixes

tasks.task: Set up tests and CI for a project with none

items.when: First, to list every page, part and endpoint and what is tested and what is not
When the project has no browser tests, to install Playwright with a config and a sample test
When tests exist but run only on a laptop, to get a pipeline file that runs them on each push
When the setup works and the first real tests must cover the riskiest rules

tasks.task: Pin current behaviour with tests before a refactor

items.when: When the code has no tests, to add them in safe steps before anything is changed
When you write tests that record what the code does today, odd cases included
When the refactor is one big step, to split tidying from behaviour change

tasks.task: Check a site or store against its spec before launch

items.when: When you have the spec and the site, to get pass or fail results with screenshots
When you want one pass over pages, links and forms at a depth you choose
When the launch is an online store, to check go-live and re-check after each fix
Before go-live, to check HTTPS, security headers and exposed secrets

tasks.task: Explore a build by hand and log what breaks

items.when: Before the session, to pick the risky areas worth an hour of free exploring
When the app runs locally, to try its screens in a real browser with screenshots and logs
When a page misbehaves, to see the real errors, network calls and slow spots
When the session ends, to turn rough notes into reports with steps and evidence

tasks.task: Plan a speed or load test

items.when: When a site or API needs a repeatable load test with baselines and ranked bottlenecks
When slow pages keep shipping, to add a speed check that blocks them in the pipeline
When one page is slow, to find the calls and scripts that hold it up

tasks.task: Run basic security checks on an app you own

items.when: When the app is running and you may test it, to find weaknesses by safe probing
When you have the API routes, to check sign-in, access rules and input handling
When you want a quick checklist pass, not a full test

tasks.task: Create safe, realistic test data

items.when: When staging needs realistic, repeatable rows loaded into its tables
When a test needs a fake file with set columns and rules, as CSV, JSON or SQL
When evidence from real accounts must be shared, to mask personal details first

tasks.task: Test an AI feature or chatbot

items.when: When a feature gives AI answers, to plan scored tests and human review
When answers must be graded the same way each run, to write the scoring guide
When the feature is an agent that takes actions, to get a test set and a release memo
When a prompt changes, to run a fixed set of cases and see what got better or worse
When a support bot gave wrong answers, to list them and write retest cases
When scores look fine but real answers are poor, to read actual examples first

tasks.task: Find why a bug escaped and stop it coming back

items.when: When the same kind of bug keeps returning, to check a chain of whys against the facts
When a bug caused an outage, to write a blameless timeline, causes and follow-up actions
When the cause is known, to add the missing check to what is re-tested each release

tasks.task: Run a small usability or user acceptance test

items.when: When three users can spare a morning, to plan tasks, a script and a fix list
When the client's own staff will run the checks and need plain pass or fail steps
When the tasks you set would lead the user to the answer

tasks.task: Move tests to a new framework

items.when: When Cypress or Selenium tests must move to Playwright, file by file
After the move, to check the new tests did not carry over old bad habits

always.when: Before any screenshot or log leaves the team, to mask personal details and keys
Before you hand over, to check your own output against every point in the request

helpers.when: When a bug needs a code fix, or the code must change before it can be tested
When tests need a pipeline, test environments or deploy checks you cannot set up alone
When the job is a full accessibility audit and statement, not one test pass
When testing finds a security hole or the client needs a real security review
When testers pass the feature but real users still cannot finish the task
When an AI feature fails its tests and the prompt, model or retrieval must change

gaps: No library item runs an exploratory testing session: charters, timed notes and a session report
No library item writes spreadsheet-ready manual test cases for a form or a release regression checklist; only the kit prompts do
No library item tests a mobile app on real devices or plans a device and OS matrix
No library item compares screenshots between releases to catch visual changes
No library item writes a load test script; the library only plans the test
No library item masks or scrambles personal data in a database copy for testing; only screenshots are covered
No library item checks how an email renders across mail apps
No library item reports quality over time: escaped bugs, flaky rate, time to fix
No library item tests a translated app for clipped text, date formats and right-to-left layout
The mutation check and suite audit in the library are for Python only; other languages have no equal
